v5.title: Architect
v5.subtitle: Follow the questions to find the right eAuction type
v5.q1: Does the spend justify a real-time eAuction?
v5.q2: Do you have 3+ suppliers with close prices?
v5.q3: Do you want to award directly from the eAuction?
v5.iClick: Click YES or NO to navigate the tree
v5.iDone: Recommendation found — reset to explore again
v5.dsShort: Combines English + Dutch for maximum competition
v5.dsDesc: The most powerful format. An English phase drives prices down and narrows the field. Then a Dutch phase starts far below the English best price and ascends — only the top 3 suppliers compete, and the first to accept wins. Two-stage pressure extracts the true price floor.
v5.dsUse: Ideal when you have many competitive suppliers and want to extract maximum value.
v5.enShort: Suppliers compete by lowering prices in real time
v5.enDesc: Suppliers bid against each other in real time, driving prices down. Supports overtime extensions, preference weighting, and ceiling prices. The most flexible format.
v5.enUse: Best when you have 3+ competitive suppliers and want full control over options.
v5.duShort: Price ascends each round, first to accept wins
v5.duDesc: Price starts low and rises automatically over time. The first supplier to accept the current price wins the lot. Supports pre-bids for scheduled automatic bidding.
v5.duUse: Use when you want a binding award and have a known market price.
v5.jpShort: Price descends each round, last remaining supplier wins
v5.jpDesc: Price starts high and decreases round by round. Suppliers must confirm each round or exit when too low. The last supplier standing wins. Great for price discovery.
v5.jpUse: Use when you don't need a binding award and want to discover the true market price.
v5.sbDesc: Each supplier submits one sealed offer without seeing other bids. Simple, fast, and requires minimal supplier engagement. No live interaction needed.
v5.sbUse: Use when the spend is small or suppliers won't participate in a live eAuction.
v5.trDesc: Traditional direct negotiation with suppliers. No eAuction platform involved. Use when competitive tension isn't possible or the category doesn't suit an eAuction format.
v5.trUse: Use when you have very few suppliers or the spend doesn't justify an electronic process.

hiw.overviewDesc: Crown Architect is an AI-powered tool that analyses your procurement context and recommends the best eAuction strategy. It evaluates 22 possible strategies across 6 dimensions to find the optimal match for each lot.
hiw.familiesIntro: eAuction types are ranked from most efficient (highest savings potential) to most accessible. The engine evaluates which eAuction type best fits your context.
hiw.legendDesc: Short description of how this eAuction type works
hiw.legendOptions: Available configuration options for this type
hiw.legendClick: Click any card to see full details
hiw.scoringIntro: Each lot is scored across 6 dimensions. The engine combines your answers with a scoring matrix to compute a compatibility percentage for each of 22 strategies.
hiw.scoringMatch: The compatibility % shows how well a strategy fits your context compared to the best possible match.
hiw.scoringElimination: Strategies incompatible with your inputs are automatically eliminated (e.g. English eAuctions require ranking, Double Scenario needs 3+ suppliers).
hiw.dim4Desc: Bonus or malus applied to a supplier's offer based on quality, relationship, or other criteria
hiw.conceptPreBidDesc: Offer submitted by a supplier before the live eAuction begins. During the live eAuction, this bid is executed automatically.
hiw.conceptPreferenceDesc: Bonus or malus applied to a supplier's offer based on quality, relationship, or other criteria. Can be non-financial (qualitative) or financial (price-based).
hiw.conceptAwardingDesc: How the winner is determined: Award (binding, best price wins), Rank (ordered but not binding), or No Rank (market testing only).
hiw.conceptIntensityDesc: The competitive pressure level: Collaborative, Competitive, High, or Intense.
hiw.conceptEliminationDesc: Some eAuction types are incompatible with certain inputs. For example, 'No Rank' eliminates English and Double Scenario. Spend under 100K eliminates most live formats.
hiw.scoringTableIntro: Which options are available for each eAuction type:
hiw.exampleDs: e.g. 500 laptops, 5 suppliers, simple specs — maximum savings via English + Dutch rounds.
hiw.exampleEn: e.g. office furniture, 4 suppliers, binding award — real-time bidding with ceiling price.
hiw.exampleDu: e.g. fleet vehicles, 3 suppliers, known market price — ascending price until first acceptance.
hiw.exampleJp: e.g. raw materials, 6 suppliers, price discovery — descending rounds reveal true market price.
hiw.exampleSb: e.g. consulting services, 2 suppliers, no live eAuction — single sealed submission.
hiw.exampleTr: e.g. specialised equipment, 1 supplier — direct negotiation off-platform.
hiw.illustDs: Two-round strategy: English eAuction then Dutch round for maximum savings
hiw.illustEn: Suppliers compete in real-time by lowering their price until no one bids further
hiw.illustDu: Price starts low and rises automatically — first supplier to accept wins
hiw.illustJp: Price drops each round — suppliers exit when it's too low, last one standing wins
hiw.illustSb: Each supplier submits one sealed bid — no one sees others' prices
hiw.illustTr: Direct negotiation with the supplier — no eAuction mechanism
hiw.faq1Q: Can I change the eAuction type after eAuction has been created?
hiw.faq1A: Yes — you can re-run the Architect at any time to get a new recommendation. Your previous configuration is saved.
hiw.faq2Q: What happens if no supplier bids?
hiw.faq2A: The event closes without a winner. You can then adjust the eAuction parameters and strategy (ie. eAuction type or competitive intensity) and relaunch the negotiation.
hiw.faq3Q: How are the estimated savings calculated?
hiw.faq3A: The percentages are based on historical data across thousands of eAuctions. Actual savings depend on market conditions, supplier competition, and your negotiation leverage.
hiw.faq4Q: Do suppliers need to be registered before creating the eAuction?
hiw.faq4A: No — you can invite suppliers after creating the eAuction. However, the recommendation accuracy improves when you know the exact number of participants.
hiw.lvlPreBidEnabledDesc: Suppliers can submit an offer before the eAuction starts
hiw.lvlPreBidDisabledDesc: Suppliers place their bid during the live eAuction only
hiw.lvlPrefNoneDesc: All suppliers compete on equal footing
hiw.lvlPrefNonFinDesc: Qualitative criteria (quality, CSR, delivery) weighted alongside price
hiw.lvlPrefFinDesc: Price handicap or advantage applied to preferred suppliers
hiw.lvlPrefFinOnlyNote: Financial preference only — qualitative (non-financial) weighting is not supported for this eAuction type.
hiw.lvlAwardAwardDesc: Contract awarded at the end of the eAuction
hiw.lvlAwardNoRankDesc: Result visible to buyer only — no feedback to suppliers
hiw.lvlIntCollabDesc: Light pressure — suited for strategic partnerships
hiw.lvlIntCompetDesc: Balanced competition — works with most market configurations
hiw.lvlIntHighDesc: Strong pressure — real-time bidding drives prices down
hiw.lvlIntAggrDesc: Full competitive pressure — maximises savings potential
hiw.noOptions: No configurable parameters — this format is fully managed off-platform.
hiw.optPreBidOnInfo: Suppliers submit a price before the eAuction opens. This pre-bid runs automatically at start, setting the initial competitive position.
hiw.optPreBidOffInfo: This eAuction type does not support pre-bids. All prices are submitted live during the eAuction.
hiw.optPrefAvailInfo: You can apply a weighting to favour certain suppliers (qualitative or financial adjustment).
hiw.optPrefNAInfo: This eAuction type does not support preference weighting.
hiw.optNoneInfo: No preference — all suppliers compete on equal footing.
hiw.optNonFinInfo: Non-financial — qualitative criteria (quality, CSR, delivery) weighted alongside price.
hiw.optFinInfo: Financial — a price adjustment (% or fixed amount) is applied to selected suppliers.
hiw.optAwardInfo: Binding — the winning supplier is contractually awarded the lot.
hiw.optRankInfo: Non-binding ranking — suppliers are ordered but no contract is signed.
hiw.optNoRankInfo: Market test only — prices collected with no ranking or commitment.
hiw.optAwardNAInfo: Traditional negotiation does not use an automated award mechanism.

auctionParams.title: Recommended Parameters
auctionParams.supplierCeilingsHint: Each supplier's current offer is used as their ceiling price
auctionParams.aboveAuctionCeiling: This price exceeds the eAuction ceiling — the supplier won't be able to bid above it
auctionParams.aboveStartingPrice: This price exceeds the starting price — the supplier has no rounds available
auctionParams.top3Note: Only top 3 suppliers from the English phase participate
auctionParams.dutchPreferredNote: Preferred supplier has exclusive access for the first 30s of each round
auctionParams.prebidRecommended: Pre-bid: recommended ON — guarantees an offer on eAuction day
auctionParams.dsParamsAfterEnglish: Parameters are set after the English phase, based on the best price achieved.
auctionParams.proposedCeilingTooltip: Suggested maximum price per supplier, based on their initial offer and market data. Suppliers cannot bid above this threshold during the eAuction.
auctionParams.proposedPrebidTooltip: Suggested sailing (pre-bid threshold) per supplier. For Dutch and Japanese auctions, all suppliers are set to the same sailing — the auction starting/ending price (lowest offer − 5%). The system auto-accepts when the auction price reaches this amount.
